{{short description|Gives a lower bound on the volume of a Riemannian manifold}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Berger's isoembolic inequality''' is a result in [[Riemannian geometry]] that gives a lower bound on the volume of a [[Riemannian manifold]] and also gives a [[necessary and sufficient condition]] for the manifold to be [[Isometry (Riemannian geometry)|isometric]] to the {{mvar|m}}-[[dimension]]al [[sphere]] with its usual "round" metric. The theorem is named after the [[mathematician]] [[Marcel Berger]], who derived it from an inequality proved by [[Jerry Kazdan]].

==Statement of the theorem==
Let {{math|(''M'',&nbsp;''g'')}} be a [[closed manifold|closed]] {{mvar|m}}-dimensional Riemannian manifold with [[injectivity radius]] {{math|inj(''M'')}}. Let {{math|vol(''M'')}} denote the Riemannian volume of {{mvar|M}} and let {{math|''c''<sub>''m''</sub>}} denote the volume of the standard {{mvar|m}}-dimensional sphere of radius one. Then

:<math>\mathrm{vol} (M) \geq c_m \left(\!\frac{\mathrm{inj}(M)}{\pi}\!\right)^{\!\!m},</math>

with equality [[if and only if]] {{math|(''M'',&nbsp;''g'')}} is isometric to the [[sphere|{{mvar|m}}-sphere]] with its usual round metric. This result is known as Berger's ''isoembolic inequality''.{{sfnm|1a1=Berger|1y=2003|1loc=Theorem 148|2a1=Chavel|2y=1984|2loc=Theorem V.22|3a1=Chavel|3y=2006|3loc=Theorem VII.2.2|4a1=Sakai|4y=1996|4loc=Theorem VI.2.1}} The proof relies upon an analytic inequality proved by Kazdan.{{sfnm|1a1=Berger|1y=2003|1loc=Lemma 158|2a1=Besse|2y=1978|2loc=Appendix E|3a1=Chavel|3y=1984|3loc=Theorem V.1|4a1=Chavel|4y=2006|4loc=Theorem VII.2.1|5a1=Sakai|5y=1996|5loc=Proposition VI.2.2}} The original work of Berger and Kazdan appears in the appendices of [[Arthur Besse]]'s book "Manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed." At this stage, the isoembolic inequality appeared with a non-optimal constant.{{sfnm|1a1=Besse|1y=1978|1loc=Appendix D}} Sometimes Kazdan's inequality is called ''Berger–Kazdan inequality''.{{sfnm|1a1=Chavel|1y=1984|1loc=Theorem V.1}}
